bull.b: Growing Elfabrio sales alongside additional geographic and dosing approvals can broaden the product’s commercial reach and improve recurring product-related economics. The regulatory progress supports deeper penetration of the Fabry market and strengthens Protalix’s established partnered product franchise over the coming quarters.

Positive earnings, strong operating margins, and a debt-free balance sheet give Protalix greater capacity to fund operations and advance its pipeline internally. Current liquidity also reduces financing pressure, while improved profitability provides a stronger base for sustaining investment through future development cycles.

A proprietary expression platform spanning development and manufacturing gives Protalix an integrated foundation for producing recombinant biologics, particularly in rare diseases. This capability can support repeated product development and partnered supply opportunities rather than relying on a single commercial asset.

bear.b: Reliance on a major commercialization partner and uneven purchasing patterns can make reported revenue difficult to forecast from quarter to quarter. This volatility may obscure underlying product demand, complicate planning, and increase dependence on partner inventory decisions for near-term operating performance.

The large milestone materially boosted first-half revenue but does not represent a recurring sales stream. Comparisons may weaken when similar payments are absent, making current growth and profitability less representative of ongoing product economics and increasing the importance of sustained Elfabrio sales.

High observed anti-drug antibody incidence and unresolved dose or regimen selection create meaningful uncertainty for PRX-115’s development path. Immunogenicity and infusion-related reaction concerns could require further optimization, affect timelines, and limit the program’s eventual commercial positioning.
